correctness.rationale: For any forbidden labeled set of b<n vertices, each uniform-start q-holding walk avoids it with probability ((n-b)/n)(1-(1-q)b/(n-1))^t; every exterior site has the same per-step survival probability. Independent walks multiply these factors, giving ((n-b)/n)^k alpha_b^T, exactly the avoidance probability of one T-step walk augmented with k-1 independent uniform vertices. Every labeled-set avoidance probability agrees, and finite Boolean-lattice inversion proves the full random-set identity. Its inclusion coupling and the factorial-moment formulas are exact. Boundary cases n=2, k=1, T=0, q=0 or 1, and b=n are checked. The independent exact-rational checker at check.py passes 5,560 finite state and combinatorial comparisons; they do not replace the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary study states expected-range collaboration and asks for quantitative difference and stochastic dominance; it does not present the stronger exact labeled random-set law, lifetime-allocation invariance or independent seed augmentation. Broad multiple-walker cover-time work bounds completion rather than proving a finite-time set-law identity, and a 2026 paper treats a single walker on a complete network, not multiwalker augmentation. Full accessible primary preprint and focused comparison sections were read. A more general unindexed finite-state coupon-collector theorem or inaccessible journal text could alter historical priority; independent confirmation remains necessary.
residual_risks: The 2025 journal version of Dey–Kim–Terlov was not accessible in full; accessible first preprint was read.
An unindexed classical coupon-collector, restart, or finite-chain identity could independently contain the same seed-augmentation law.
Theorem is specific to uniform-start identically parametrized complete-graph walks; it does not settle general-graph stochastic domination.

value.rationale: The identity answers the canonical K_n specialization of a published quantitative-collaboration question and a published stochastic-dominance question, strengthening both to equality of complete labeled-set laws. It gives exact finite-size gap, full distribution, all uncovered factorial moments, and provable invariance under allocation of a fixed transition budget. A path counterexample establishes a meaningful noncomplete boundary and shows the structural phenomenon is not tautological. Its scope is a natural benchmark graph class rather than an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
